checklist_item: Consistency with prior plans such as the district unit plan
checkpoints: Confirm consistency between the environmental impact assessment and the district unit plan || Confirm the building limit line, maximum number of floors, floor height restriction, etc. || Confirm parking count, buffer green space, agreement of the perpendicular layout, low-rise placement zones, etc.
additional_comment: For site entrances and similar plan elements, coordinate with the department responsible for higher-level plans such as the traffic impact assessment and incorporate the agreed adjustments where necessary.

checklist_item: Provision of dwelling units for the housing vulnerable in rental housing
checkpoints: Apply 8% or more in the Seoul metropolitan area and 5% or more in provincial areas
basis: Enforcement Decree of the Housing-Vulnerable Support Act, Article 5

checklist_item: Appropriateness of gate post planning at the main site entrance
checkpoints: Provide sufficient separation between the crosswalk and the gate post to secure sight lines for pedestrian protection || Secure a sidewalk width of 1.5m or more beside internal roads and install a road 7m or wider including the sidewalk || Secure a gate post height of 4.5m or more where fire truck access is considered || Install a pedestrian barrier fence between the gate post columns
additional_comment: Gate post height: 4m under the legal standard, 4.5m under the internal standard, and 5m per the National Fire Agency standard manual
other: Improve the design, for example with a safety fence, so pedestrians cannot walk between the gate post columns
basis: Site Quality Control Team-1961 ('15.6.29) · Standard Manual for Processing Consent for Building Permits, etc. ('23.12, National Fire Agency) · Design Guideline Article 14 (p. 48)

checklist_item: Appropriateness of vehicle access planning at the site entrance
checkpoints: Secure the driveway width in consideration of the 0.5m installation width of the barrier gate base pad || Locate the access control system on the driver's side (left in the direction of travel) || Install the visitor lane facing the guard booth so that it is visible from the booth || Separate the access lanes for residents and visitors || Where there are 3 or fewer entry/exit lanes, plan reversible entry and exit lanes
additional_comment: To prevent complaints about vehicle congestion, secure a vehicle queuing space from the barrier gate sized for 2 compact cars (approx. 10m)
other: Where the traffic impact assessment requires a change to the entry/exit lane plan, coordinate with the relevant department and incorporate it

checklist_item: Appropriateness of planning for children's school-vehicle stops
checkpoints: Install a median at the main entrance or a roundabout so that school vehicles can stop || Separate the circulation routes of general vehicles and school vehicles (planting bed recommended) || Install pavement markings and signage to identify the school-vehicle stop || Do not plan the stop where a crosswalk is installed || Install safety facilities such as convex mirrors and vehicle-exit warning signs where necessary || Where a kids station is installed, review sight lines to the stop
additional_comment: Install a low planting bed inside the roundabout to prevent accidents caused by driver blind spots when reversing
basis: Rule on Housing Construction Standards, Article 6 · Regulation on Housing Construction Standards, Article 26

drawing: Site layout plan / Building floor plan
checklist_item: Installation of falling-object protection at entrances
checkpoints: Residential tower piloti with open top, underground parking ramp: 1,000mm || Roof-level entrance door: 900mm || Residential tower entrance, outdoor stair: 600mm (at least 2 stair risers from the entrance)
additional_comment: Design-driven planning may shorten the canopy projection in some areas, so review this in advance
basis: Design Guideline Article 14 (p. 22)

drawing: Site layout plan / DA (supply/exhaust vent) detail
checklist_item: Fall-prevention planning for above-ground structures
checkpoints: Plan fall prevention for above-ground structures such as top lights and D.A || (Fan room ventilation opening) Installing a safety railing on the inner side is recommended || (Underground parking ventilation opening) Install galvanized steel grating || (Underground parking ventilation opening) Install planting 1m or wider, or a safety fence or railing
additional_comment: Do not use fall-prevention netting or wire; install steel grating
basis: Design Guideline Article 44 (p. 186) · Detail drawings DA83-401~404

checklist_item: Prohibition of structures in front of lower-floor dwelling units
checkpoints: Avoid placing D.A in front of the units || Avoid placing the household resource storage in front of the units || Avoid placing other facilities such as bicycle storage in front of the units
additional_comment: Review relocating these facilities to the side or rear so that they do not obstruct views from lower-floor units
other: Use piloti space for outdoor bicycle storage where possible

drawing: Site layout plan / Exterior stair plan and section
checklist_item: Confirmation of the outdoor elevator installation plan
checkpoints: Install a canopy above the landing and partitions at the sides || Raise the entrance floor by 15cm and finish it with flame-textured granite || For accessibility, provide a ramp of 1/12 or flatter and tactile dot blocks || Use tempered glass 12mm or thicker from handrail height for the glazing that provides the car's outward view
additional_comment: Reinforce the detail drawings, including the tempered glass of the car
basis: Housing Design Division 1-4387 ('10.12.22.) · LHCS 31 55 05 15 Observation elevator

checklist_item: Plan to secure access lanes for moving trucks
checkpoints: Secure access lanes for moving trucks, considering units that will not use a ladder truck (secure a lane 4m wide, at least 3m, up to the residential tower entrance)
additional_comment: Plan the access road width considering the 2.3m cargo bed width of a 5-ton truck

checklist_item: Installation of traffic safety facilities around the underground parking ramp
checkpoints: Plan traffic safety facilities such as vehicle-exit warning signs at the ramp entrance || Provide a buffer zone where the underground parking garage merges onto the above-ground road || Install safety facilities including convex mirrors, speed humps and pavement markings (stop line)
additional_comment: Separate the exit from the above-ground road with curbs, landscaping and similar measures so that vehicles do not merge directly onto the road

checklist_item: Underground parking ramp layout plan
checkpoints: Avoid locating the ramp entrance in front of dwelling units || Use landscaping and similar measures to prevent complaints about headlight light pollution and alarm noise
additional_comment: Also for deck parking access, check the vehicle circulation route and take measures so that lower-floor units are not affected by vehicle entry

checklist_item: Underground interference in urban construction planning
checkpoints: Offset underground structures at least 1m from the adjacent lot boundary || Design underground structures in consideration of constructability and interference with adjacent buildings
additional_comment: When reviewing the site layout plan, check the adjacent lot boundary to identify and address issues in advance

checklist_item: Site planning in consideration of earth retaining and excavation
checkpoints: Apply conventional earth retaining methods such as H-beam with timber lagging or earth anchors || Do not use earth anchors where the area outside the site is another use || Install rakers toward the inside of the site || Prevent interference between rakers and underground structures || Where rakers inevitably interfere with underground structures, coordinate across the architectural, civil and structural disciplines to minimize section loss and damage to waterproofing

drawing: Site layout plan / Composite design drawing
checklist_item: Appropriateness of the stormwater handling plan
checkpoints: Confirm the final stormwater routing from buildings and do not route stormwater pipes along pedestrian paths || Review slopes and trenches so that standing water does not occur || Review the suitability of stormwater trench locations (apartment buildings, auxiliary welfare facilities, etc.)
additional_comment: Check the slope and trench plan at auxiliary building entrances and prevent stormwater from flowing in via reverse slope

checklist_item: Confirmation of level markings and suitability at level differences
checkpoints: Mark levels on slopes and at level differences || Where a height difference occurs, secure the slope setback distance (confirm slope setback, landscape rock stacking, etc.)
additional_comment: Beyond the main entrance, identify sections where stormwater could flow from the road into the site, and review installing flood barriers and upsizing drainage channels where necessary

drawing: Site layout plan / Auxiliary facility plan
checklist_item: Appropriateness of neighborhood living facility planning
checkpoints: Plan a household resource storage for residents only in the neighborhood living facility || Provide a clear corridor width of 1,200mm or more and install a ramp where floor level differences occur || Provide at least 1 accessible parking space || Take measures such as planting to block noise and odors and for landscaping || Install an access opening and inspection ladder below the 1st-floor restroom || Provide a clear pit height of 1,800mm or more and a clear passage of 1,200mm or more
additional_comment: Items that cannot be confirmed on the site layout plan shall be reviewed with reference to the auxiliary facility design drawings
basis: Design Guideline (Architecture) Article 33 (p. 162)

drawing: Site layout plan / Building floor plan / Core floor plan
checklist_item: Confirmation of slopes (gradient, pitch) by location
checkpoints: Ramp [residential tower entrance: 1/12 (housing vulnerable: 1/18), auxiliary welfare facilities: 1/12] || Roof [pitched roof: 4/10, flat roof: 1/50~1/150] || Dwelling unit [bathroom: 1/100, balcony: 1/150] || Common area [corridor: 1/150] || Underground [underground parking garage: confirm adequate slope where trenches are installed]
basis: Roof — Design Guideline Article 17 (pp. 101, 102) · Corridor, entrance — Design Guideline Article 14 (pp. 41, 20) · Bathroom — Design Guideline Article 15 (p. 51) · Auxiliary welfare — Design Guideline Article 26 (p. 131)

checklist_item: Confirmation of drawing consistency between disciplines at key locations
checkpoints: Confirm consistency among architectural, structural, civil, landscape and electrical drawings at key locations || Compare the structural frame with the design member sizes || Confirm whether structural calculations account for the landscaping soil depth || Confirm consistency between exterior drawings and electrical drawings for side walls, gate posts, building entrances and basement connecting passages

checklist_item: Ensuring equity with adjacent sites in the same district
checkpoints: Confirm that separate survey data such as the total design study has been prepared and submitted || Extent of stone finishes, stone type, landscape lighting, railing material outside the site || Confirm finishes at the main entrance, storage space by balcony unit type (shoe cabinet, built-in closet, etc.), options, etc.
additional_comment: Plan in advance so that differences in design and finishes between sites in the district do not generate complaints

drawing: Fire compartment plan / Building floor plan
checklist_item: Confirmation of whether fire compartment drawings have been prepared
checkpoints: Prepare separate detail drawings, including a fire compartment plan for each building || Indicate fire compartments including fire doors, automatic fire shutters and fire dampers || Indicate the egress distance from the living room to the fire door
additional_comment: For apartment buildings, confirm an egress distance of 40m, or 50m for buildings of 16 stories or more
basis: Design Guideline (Architecture) Article 11 (p. 7)

checklist_item: Confirmation of the final area calculation table
checkpoints: Review the calculation formulas and values, and verify in CAD where necessary || Confirm that the figures in the area calculation table match the dwelling unit floor plans
basis: Design Guideline (Architecture) Article 22 (p. 127)

drawing: Interior finish schedule / Main entrance plan
checklist_item: Design standard for common-area floor finishes
checkpoints: Indoor common-area floor finish: honed granite (residential tower above-ground entrance lobby, basement connecting passage, EV hall, public buildings, auxiliary facilities, etc.)
basis: Housing Innovation Office-1483 (2025.04.15.)

checklist_item: Finishes specified for stairwell walls and baseboards
checkpoints: Delete the resin plaster specification on stairwell walls where aluminum (AL) formwork is applied || Apply resin plaster to the wall where the elevator is installed in the EV hall || Where concrete surfaces receive a paint finish, specify 'baseboard paint' (do not use cove base paint)
basis: In preparation for defect litigation · Customer Quality Innovation Team-6399 ('20.12.10) · Customer Quality Innovation Team-4381 ('20.09.07) · DA-70-107~109

checklist_item: Confirmation of finishes in the basement EV hall and connecting passage
checkpoints: (Ceiling) Light-gauge steel ceiling frame + color aluminum ceiling panel || (Wall) Apply materials such as multicolor pattern paint or porcelain tile that resist condensation and moisture, are easy to maintain and provide fire performance
basis: Housing Innovation Office-1483 (2025.04.15.)

drawing: Interior finish schedule / Seasonal storage section
checklist_item: Confirmation of the ceiling finish standard for seasonal storage
checkpoints: (Ceiling) Interior water-based paint on concrete, or THK10 inorganic spray coating on insulation areas || (Wall) Interior water-based paint on concrete
basis: Customer Quality Innovation Team-6399 ('20.12.10)

drawing: Interior finish schedule / Core floor plan
checklist_item: Confirmation of the ceiling finish standard for elevator halls
checkpoints: (1st floor) Light-gauge steel ceiling frame + color aluminum ceiling panel || (2nd floor and above) Concrete substrate + multicolor pattern paint (if SP piping unavoidably passes through the elevator hall because of the AV room layout, apply light-gauge steel ceiling frame + 1 layer of THK12.5 gypsum board + joint treatment + multicolor pattern paint)
additional_comment: If SP piping is exposed along only part of the corridor, for-sale housing cannot easily vary the ceiling finish, so apply the light-gauge steel ceiling frame + gypsum board throughout
basis: Customer Quality Innovation Team-5236 ('22.12.05) · Customer Quality Innovation Team-6539 ('20.12.16) · Customer Quality Innovation Team-7891 ('19.12.23)

drawing: Interior finish schedule / Insulation and waterproofing detail
checklist_item: Verify bathroom wall waterproofing finish criteria
checkpoints: Masonry wall areas: cement liquid waterproofing or polymer-based waterproofing + tile adhesive mortar + ceramic tile || Bathroom waterproofing on masonry walls up to H=1200mm; shower stall wall side up to H=1800mm || Where the bathroom wall is concrete, delete wall waterproofing
additional_comment: When wall waterproofing is deleted, also delete cement liquid waterproofing (or polymer-based waterproofing, H=1200mm or less) and 8mm tile adhesive mortar (from H=1200mm up to ceiling +100mm)
basis: Customer Quality Innovation Group-6959 ('18.12.20) · DA-15-308, 309

drawing: Interior finish schedule / Dwelling unit floor plan
checklist_item: Verify finish criteria at kitchen cabinet installation areas
checkpoints: (Base cabinet floor) Apply water-based paint (interior grade) up to the cabinet end line at base cabinet locations, and note on the drawing that flooring (sheet carpet/hardwood plywood floor) is installed 100mm inward from the cabinet end line || (Base cabinet wall) Omit finish material on walls at kitchen cabinet locations, and note on the drawing that kitchen wall tile is installed 100mm inward from the end of the base cabinet rear shelf || Base cabinet toe kick: note on the drawing that it is installed 60mm inward from the cabinet end line
basis: Housing Technology Division-5545 ('22.11.17)

checklist_item: Secure fire-resistive structure in the wall beside the unit entrance fire door frame
checkpoints: (Stair-access type) Mortar pack between fire door frame (unit entrance door, refuge area, etc.) and structural frame || (Corridor-access type) Urethane foam pack between general door frame (condensation-resistant unit entrance door, etc.) and structural frame || Provide 100mm wall thickness beside the fire door frame and apply fire gasket || Indoor side: install gypsum board furring, then apply 15X15 square sealant || Outdoor side: apply 10X10 triangular sealant || Refuge area and common areas: apply 10X10 triangular sealant on both indoor and outdoor sides
additional_comment: Fire doors in stair-access apartments must have fire gaskets installed; corridor-access apartments use EPDM gaskets
basis: DA-96-513 · Housing Technology Division-598 ('19.3.4) · Customer Quality Innovation Group-7891 ('19.12.23)

drawing: Dwelling unit floor plan / Dwelling unit window schedule
checklist_item: Verify unit entrance door performance
checkpoints: (Corridor type) Condensation resistance + airtightness || (Stair-core type) Condensation resistance + fire resistance + smoke control + airtightness
basis: LHCS 41 55 06 Steel windows and doors

drawing: Dwelling unit floor plan / Main section / Waterproofing and insulation detail
checklist_item: Plan flanking resilient layer for inter-floor noise
checkpoints: Flanking resilient layer thickness 10mm or more || Show the flanking resilient layer on all walls so the finish mortar does not contact walls directly || Install continuously at flanking areas in contact with the ondol floor, such as masonry walls, load-bearing walls, and living room PL window frames || Do not install at door frame bottoms (support block installation) or entrance door areas

drawing: Dwelling unit floor plan / Main section / Waterproofing and insulation detail
checklist_item: Apply Grade 2 inter-floor noise technology
checkpoints: (110mm floor structure) Composite resilient layer 30 + general mortar 40 + general mortar 40 (composite resilient layer, thermal conductivity 0.036 W/m·K or less) || Meet the thermal transmittance criterion of 0.810 W/m·K for heated inter-floor slabs || (Structural design) Where general mortar is substituted, reflect the increased unit weight in the structural design
additional_comment: Where lightweight foamed concrete is applied, use the 0.6-grade quality standard, and 0.5 grade in Central Region 1
basis: Smart Housing Technology Division-1299 ('25.03.28)

drawing: Dwelling unit floor plan / Interior finish schedule / Window detail
checklist_item: Verify adequacy of unit bathroom door planning
checkpoints: Plan so the door leaf does not conflict with the toilet when the bathroom door is opened/closed (also review when a bidet is installed) || Bathroom door size: change 7X21/D to 8X21/D || Finish: decorative sheet over ABS
additional_comment: Where the highest building in the complex is 16 storeys or more, install door finger-pinch guards on bathroom doors (2 indoor faces)
basis: Customer Quality Innovation Group-4381 ('20.09.07) · Public Housing Planning Division-2274 (2022.06.22.)

checklist_item: Plan same-storey piping space for system bathroom
checkpoints: Prefabricated bathrooms in public rental housing shall use same-storey wall piping || Install semi-one-piece wall-drain water closet || Bathroom slab thickness 150mm with 90mm slab down || Slab width at the step offset bend shall be 315mm or more (400mm recommended) || Provide 180mm or more clearance from the UBR wall end to the inside face of the lightweight partition || Provide waterproof board width of 1500mm or more to avoid conflict between the water closet and door
additional_comment: Same-storey wall piping does not require a fire-stop filling structure, so there is no need to change to wet construction
basis: Public Housing Facilities Division-6860 ('24.11.12)

drawing: Dwelling unit floor plan / Main section / Waterproofing and insulation detail
checklist_item: Review bathroom ceiling insulation and condensation
checkpoints: Typical floor bathrooms shall be heated, with THK35 insulation installed under the slab (delete ceiling condensation-prevention material in bathrooms with insulation) || System bathrooms shall be unheated, with no insulation installed
basis: Customer Quality Innovation Group-7891 ('19.12.23) · Design Guideline (Architecture) Article 15 (p.59)

checklist_item: Verify adequacy of bathroom shower stall planning
checkpoints: Check interference of the shower stall door leaf with the faucet and handle when opening/closing || Plan the shower area 900*900mm or larger || Where the shower area is 900*900mm or less, install the partition only (delete the door leaf) || Shower stall glass: laminated glass THK 8.76 or more, Class II-1 or II-2 || Apply floor coil heating to the shower stall as well || Prepare a shower area step detail and note the shower stall glass (raised installation) || Install 1 floor drain trench in the bathroom
basis: Customer Quality Innovation Group-2029 (2018.04.24) · Housing Technology Division-2166 ('18.06.11) · Housing Technology Division-3741 ('15.10.16.) · Design Guideline (Architecture) Article 15 (p.61) · DA-92-015

drawing: Dwelling unit floor plan / Interior (bathroom, living room, etc.)
checklist_item: Verify adequacy of tile planning at dissimilar-material joints
checkpoints: Avoid designing dissimilar materials (concrete + masonry/lightweight partition) on bathroom walls, art walls, etc. || Plan dissimilar-material joints on the tile layout S.P (Start Point) grid || Install movement joints at crack-prone locations (dissimilar-material joints, S.P locations) to prevent cracking
additional_comment: Tile cracking occurs from minor shrinkage and movement of the substrate at joints between dissimilar materials such as masonry and concrete, so install movement joints (caulking, etc.) and reflect them in the S.P
basis: Customer Quality Innovation Group-5235 (21.12.02)

checklist_item: Minimize masonry walls
checkpoints: Minimize masonry walls and use reinforced concrete || Avoid short wall segments at door frame wing walls (bathroom and bedroom doors, hinge side) || Delete the 80mm masonry soldier-course wall at door corners || Apply door stoppers to prevent door lock interference
additional_comment: Masonry work risks schedule delay and quality loss due to the shortage of skilled workers, so change to structural concrete where possible
basis: Customer Quality Innovation Group-6959 ('18.12.20)

checklist_item: Reinforcement plan for living room lightweight partition
checkpoints: Note steel plate reinforcement locations on the drawing where heavy items such as TVs are installed on lightweight partitions || Place 1.2mm thick, 300~600mm steel plate between base gypsum board and finish gypsum board, fixed with studs for reinforcement || No separate reinforcement required for concrete walls
additional_comment: When installing an air conditioner or wall-mounted TV on a lightweight partition, note steel plate reinforcement locations on the drawing in accordance with the specification
other: Notify residents in advance through the resident guide of reinforcement locations for fixture installation and the related installation methods
basis: LHCS 41 51 04 05 Gypsum board composite panel

drawing: Dwelling unit floor plan / Building floor plan
checklist_item: Verify adequacy of main apartment floor plan
checkpoints: Avoid excessive facade projections and recesses when planning the unit floor plan || Ensure the east-side balcony does not set back excessively compared with the west side of the front facade || Show the entire plan at side walls, staggered units, and mixed configurations where different unit types are adjacent
additional_comment: Reflect the residential tower elevation design in the facade, while avoiding excessive projections and recesses so as to secure good sunlight and daylight
basis: Design Guideline Article 15 (p.51)

drawing: Dwelling unit floor plan / Interior (kitchen cabinets)
checklist_item: Secure clearance between kitchen cooktop and wall
checkpoints: (Rental) 150mm or more from the wall (except where the total kitchen cabinet length is less than 2,500mm) || (For-sale) 150mm or more from the tiled wall || (For-sale) 300mm or more from the finished face of the cabinet side panel
additional_comment: Avoid designing a PL window behind the cooktop to prevent window deformation from heat
basis: Design Guideline Article 15 (p.57) · Customer Quality Innovation Group-4354 ('20.09.04)

drawing: Dwelling unit floor plan / Interior (kitchen cabinets)
checklist_item: Secure clearance between sink drainboard and cooktop
checkpoints: (Basic) 500mm or more recommended || (Rental) 400mm or more || (For-sale) 600mm or more (450mm or more for L-shaped cabinets)
basis: Technical Standards Division-5780 ('12.12.27.)

checklist_item: Verify kitchen lighting switch location
checkpoints: Review the installation location of the network switch for kitchen and dining lighting || Lighting switches cannot be installed on the refrigerator cabinet side panel, so relocate them to a wall such as a lightweight partition || Switches cannot be installed on cabinet side panels such as the refrigerator cabinet || Install switches on lightweight partitions 145mm or more thick
basis: Customer Quality Innovation Group-3130 ('20.07.08)

drawing: Dwelling unit floor plan / Interior (kitchen cabinets)
checklist_item: Review kitchen drain location
checkpoints: Do not install the drain at the center of the sink; offset it || Connect by the shortest route and plan so that no sag develops in the drain pipe

checklist_item: Review adequacy of small window sizes
checkpoints: Consider opening/closing defects when planning small windows in kitchens, dressing rooms, balconies, etc. || Recommended height-to-width ratio per 1 window sash: 2.5 or less
additional_comment: The ratio applies per 1 window sash, i.e. 1/2 of the width; recommended dimensions are dressing room BPW 10*12 and balcony window BP 9*10
other: Consider interference with system shelf storage when reviewing dressing room windows

checklist_item: Verify adequacy of laundry room door planning
checkpoints: Plan a turning door W=900mm or more for taking the washing machine in and out (9*21PD) || Effective clear width of the entrance door (PD, turning door) shall be W=710mm excluding the leaf and frame || Opening direction shall be toward the balcony by default, and toward the interior where not possible
additional_comment: Dimension to the inside of the door frame so that the 710mm effective clear width can be verified precisely
basis: Housing Technology Division-2112 ('20.06.25) · Design Guideline Article 15 (p.71)

checklist_item: Verify adequacy of balcony washing machine installation planning
checkpoints: Minimum effective balcony width 1000mm or more, considering the downspout || Where less than 1000mm, plan the downspout etc. behind the washing machine || Washing machine pad: 800mm wide, 1000mm deep or more || Individual heating (boiler installation): add 1000mm + 300mm or more in depth || Where a separate laundry area is partitioned within the unit, apply PVC ceiling finish
additional_comment: If the drain is located at the end between the pad and the wall, drainage becomes difficult and causes complaints such as cleaning problems, so place the drain toward the front where possible and extend the pad to the wall at the rear
basis: Design Guideline Article 15 (p.69)

drawing: Dwelling unit floor plan / Main section
checklist_item: Condensation prevention plan for non-expanded balcony
checkpoints: Wall (Zones 1, 2): 30T bead-method Type 2 Class 2 EPS + 4.5T CRC board + interior water-based paint || Wall (Zone 3): 20T bead-method Type 2 Class 2 EPS + 4.5T CRC board + interior water-based paint || Ceiling: 15T extruded-method Class 1 XPS + 9.5T gypsum board + interior water-based paint || Refuge area and outdoor unit room interior walls and ceilings: interior water-based paint finish
additional_comment: The 15T extruded-method Class 1 XPS on the ceiling is embedded in the concrete
basis: Customer Quality Innovation Group-3540 ('18.07.10) · DA60-101~106, 113, 122, 123

checklist_item: Comply with balcony drain pipe design criteria
checkpoints: Install drain pipes on walls facing the interior to prevent freezing || Drain pipe diameter in non-expanded balconies: D100
basis: Customer Quality Innovation Group-885 ('18.02.27) · Customer Quality Innovation Group-3540 ('18.07.10)

checklist_item: Verify balcony door opening direction
checkpoints: Opening direction of the non-expanded balcony folding door shall match that of the balcony window

checklist_item: Verify ABS resin vent planning
checkpoints: (Specification) ∅100 ABS resin, openable type || Install 1 unit each at the upper and lower parts of the wing walls of the front and rear balconies and refuge areas || Where a balcony boiler flue is installed, install only at the lower part of the wing wall || Also install in outdoor unit rooms with system louvers, except where the wall length is short
basis: Design Guideline (Architecture) p.106 · Customer Quality Innovation Group-1624 ('18.04.04) · Defect litigation

checklist_item: Comply with outdoor unit room design criteria
checkpoints: Secure clear space excluding the outdoor unit of 0.5m wide by 0.7m long || Plan so as not to interfere with the outdoor unit, faucets, drains, etc. || System louver: width 900mm or more, lower sill height 130mm or less || Districts with system air conditioning (for-sale, Newlywed Hope Town): outdoor unit size 950*330 || Districts with system air conditioning (for-sale, Newlywed Hope Town): required outdoor unit room area 1,450*1,030 or more
additional_comment: Determine the outdoor unit room area at the design stage in consideration of whether an outdoor unit is installed and its size
basis: Public Housing Equipment Division-1002 (2020.04.06) · Enforcement Rule of the Housing Construction Standards, Article 8

checklist_item: Comply with downward evacuation opening design criteria
checkpoints: Plan the downward evacuation opening cover to open toward the wall (do not open toward the entrance door) || Do not plan downward evacuation openings in the lowest-floor unit (including simple representation) || Where a downward evacuation opening is installed in an outdoor unit room, apply an in-swing door toward the balcony or bedroom || Installation height: tile surface +30mm or more; apply urethane membrane waterproofing at the frame joint
additional_comment: Where the lowest-floor unit of a downward evacuation route is not an evacuation floor, install an openable louver and a descent device so that evacuation is possible
other: Apply urethane membrane waterproofing (concealed) to prevent leakage
basis: Public Housing Equipment Division-1340 ('20.5.8) · Housing Technology Division-4739 ('20.12.30) · Design Guideline Article 15 (p.68)

checklist_item: Compliance with refuge area installation criteria
checkpoints: Install a refuge area where a unit on a floor of the 4th storey or higher in an apartment cannot use two or more direct stairs (not required on the 3rd storey or below / excluded where the party wall to the adjacent unit is an easily destructible lightweight structure and where a downward evacuation opening is installed) || (Area) 2㎡ or more where used separately by an individual unit / 3㎡ or more where shared with an adjacent unit || (Fire compartment) Provide as a fire compartment facing outside air and install a 60-minute+ fire door
basis: Enforcement Decree of the Building Act, Article 46, Paragraph 4 · Design Guideline Article 16 (p. 72)

checklist_item: Compliance with installation criteria for fire doors and exterior windows in refuge areas
checkpoints: For units with a refuge area on the 4th storey or higher, install a fire door (FSD) at the unit entrance and an inward-opening exterior window (PL) || Plan the fire door as an outward-opening type that swings toward the refuge area || Use a fire-rated door closer and 1.6T steel plate reinforcement on the fire door (horseshoe-type door stoppers not applied) || Plan the wall receiving the fire door in concrete (anchor installation and cracking of masonry walls) || Provide the exterior window insect screen as (type) roll type, (material) synthetic resin containing glass fiber || For 3rd-storey units equipped with a descent life line, install a steel window (SD) at the unit entrance and an inward-opening exterior window (PL) || For 1st–2nd storey units, install a steel window (SD) at the unit entrance and a sliding exterior window
basis: Housing Technology Office-4530 ('16.11.15) · Housing Technology Office-598 ('19.3.4) · Public Housing Project Office-1022 ('14.03.10) · Design Guideline Article 16 (p. 74) · DA-96-506 · DA-96-271

drawing: Dwelling unit floor plan / Building floor plan / Piloti plan / Main section
checklist_item: Review of adequacy of insulation planning for dwelling units and piloti
checkpoints: Extend the insulation so that the unit exterior wall does not come into contact with the masonry wall || Design the in-unit insulation as a continuous layer without interruption to block cold bridges and thermal bridges || Apply exterior insulation to piloti walls to maintain structural continuity with the upper dwelling units (interior insulation) || Use phenolic foam for exterior-insulated areas such as the piloti ceiling and the underside of the 1st-floor slab of auxiliary facilities
additional_comment: As exterior wall finishes must be non-combustible or quasi-non-combustible under the relevant regulations, install phenolic foam (PF board)
basis: Site Quality Management Team-4767 ('16.11.08) · Housing Technology Office-3489 (2018.09.12) · Design Guideline Article 17 (p. 92)

checklist_item: Verification of insulation planning by location, including exterior insulation
checkpoints: Where exterior insulation is applied at floor steps, extend the wall insulation down to below the floor insulation || Plan exterior insulation so that the insulation is not compromised by exterior wall finishes || Use non-combustible/quasi-non-combustible insulation such as phenolic foam for exterior insulation to prevent fire spread
additional_comment: Connect insulation facing outside air without interruption; where it is interrupted, additionally install condensation-reduction material (450mm) to prevent cold bridges
other: Where a floor-step storey occurs, consider deleting unnecessary insulation for the lower units and supplying the upper units with a different exclusive floor area
basis: Customer Quality Innovation Team-5503 (2017.12.04) · DA-60-005 · DA-60-012 · DA-60-012-1

drawing: Dwelling unit floor plan / Insulation detail
checklist_item: Verification of condensation reinforcement at exterior-wall pipe shaft (PD) locations
checkpoints: Install condensation-reduction material where a recessed niche (banchim) is installed facing an exterior-wall PD || Cabinet type: T30 extruded polystyrene foam, No. 3 || Shelf type: T30 extruded polystyrene foam No. 3 + T3 polypropylene composite insulation
additional_comment: Where the back of the recessed niche is a masonry wall, apply a 6mm base plaster or one layer of THK9.5 gypsum board; finish concrete walls exposed (no wallpaper)

drawing: Dwelling unit floor plan / Interior (shoe cabinet)
checklist_item: Verification of entrance shoe cabinet planning

basis: Customer Quality Innovation Team-2029 (2018.04.24.)

checklist_item: Verification of floor level planning for units for the mobility-impaired
checkpoints: Comply with the floor levels of the entrance, living room, and bathroom in units for the mobility-impaired || Keep the wind-stop threshold at the entrance door at 1.5cm or less, and the entrance threshold frame at 3cm or less || Considering the base frame height (10mm) of the bathroom, keep the level difference from the living room at 2cm or less || EV hall: FL+65, entrance: FL+80, living room: FL+110, bathroom: FL+90

basis: Enforcement Decree of the Act on Convenience Promotion for the Disabled, Elderly, and Pregnant Women, Appendix Table 1 · Customer Quality Innovation Team-5635 ('19.9.25)

drawing: Dwelling unit floor plan / Interior finish schedule
checklist_item: Bathroom and entrance planning for units for the mobility-impaired
checkpoints: Apply slip-resistant floor tiles in the bathroom of units for the mobility-impaired || Reflect a dynamic friction coefficient of 0.65 or more in the interior material finish schedule (0.4 for general units) || Install vertical/horizontal grab bars at the side of the entrance in units for the mobility-impaired (floor level +75~85cm)

basis: Housing Technology Office-3013 ('21.9.15) · Enforcement Decree of the Act on Convenience Promotion for the Disabled, Elderly, and Pregnant Women, Appendix Table 2 · LHCS 41 48 01 Tile Work

drawing: Building floor plan / Core floor plan
checklist_item: Review of basement drainage planning
checkpoints: Embed a drainage pipe (Ø50 PVC) at the base of the boundary wall of the basement core (connecting corridor, E/V hall, stairwell) || Install a connecting trench (W=150) from the boundary wall in the PIT to the open trench (W=600) || Route the inflow collected by the floor drain plate through the drainage pipe to connect with the connecting trench in the PIT || Connect the trench in the PIT to the sump, considering the location of the drain-down pipe of the riser

other: Verify and indicate the route from the basement core through the boundary wall, along the connecting trench in the PIT, to the sump
basis: Customer Quality Innovation Team-3130 ('20.07.08) · Design Guideline Article 14 (p. 46)

drawing: Building floor plan / Core floor plan
checklist_item: Verification of elevator lobby space planning
checkpoints: Connect the elevator to a passage accessible to persons with disabilities || Secure an elevator lobby activity space of 1,400x1,400㎜ or more in front of the E/V || Keep the gap between the lobby floor and the elevator car floor at 3cm or less
additional_comment: Provide the multi-family housing elevator as an accessible elevator, installed as close as possible to the building entrance
basis: Enforcement Rule of the Act on Convenience Promotion for the Disabled, Elderly, and Pregnant Women, Appendix Table 1

drawing: Building floor plan / Core floor plan
checklist_item: Condensation reduction in stairwells and EV halls
checkpoints: Reflect the condensation-reduction design criteria for basement stairwells and elevator halls of residential towers || In principle, plan so that the exterior walls of stairwells and EV halls do not face soil || Where unavoidable, install a DA (drainage cavity) or double wall to direct condensation
additional_comment: After installing the double wall, review the treatment and drainage plan for external inflow and condensation water
basis: Housing Design Office 2-4517 ('10.11.22)

checklist_item: Planning for directing condensation and refrigerant condensate
checkpoints: Plan an open trench and sump in the pit level to direct condensation water || Reflect the plan for directing air-conditioner refrigerant condensate || Apply a forced-exhaust wall-mounted fan to the seasonal storage (PIT area), considering constructability and economy

checklist_item: Separation planning between electrical/generator rooms and residential towers
checkpoints: Separate the electrical and generator room structure from residential towers so that noise and vibration are not transmitted || Plan a double wall where separation is not possible

checklist_item: Compliance with direct stair installation criteria
checkpoints: Install two or more direct stairs where the total living room floor area per storey is 300㎡ or more (excluding floors with 4 units or fewer) || Keep the travel distance from the living room (at the far end) to the direct stair (door) at 50m or less (40m for 16 storeys or higher) || Where two or more direct stairs are provided, separate them by at least 1/3 of the longest diagonal length of the residential tower
additional_comment: In an apartment, where a unit on the 4th storey or higher cannot use two or more direct stairs, install a refuge area on the balcony (3㎡ for shared use with an adjacent unit, 2㎡ for individual units)
other: Where sprinklers are not installed, provide two direct stairs separated by at least 1/2 of the diagonal length
basis: Enforcement Decree of the Building Act, Article 34, Paragraphs 1 and 2

checklist_item: Verification of special evacuation stair installation criteria
checkpoints: Install a special evacuation stair where the building is 16 storeys or more above ground or 3 storeys or more below ground (excluding corridor-access type without corridor windows or floors with a floor area of less than 400㎡) || Provide a vestibule (combined with the elevator lobby) with a door clear width of 0.9m or more, smoke control equipment, and a 60-minute fire door || Provide a fire elevator lobby area of 6㎡ or more per car
additional_comment: Where a special evacuation stair is required, verify that the vestibule is not omitted at the corridor end in addition to the core side
basis: Enforcement Decree of the Building Act, Article 35 · Design Guideline Article 14 (pp. 33, 34, etc.)

checklist_item: Adequate residential tower floor planning for corridor-access apartments
checkpoints: Calculate the corridor width as the actual clear walking width excluding downspouts, meters, handrails, and other installations || Secure a clear width of 1,200mm or more for single-loaded corridors || Secure a clear width of 1,800mm or more for double-loaded corridors (where living spaces face each other, regardless of the entrance) || (Privacy) Do not plan unit entrance doors facing each other (arrange diagonally) || (Privacy) Plan so that unit entrance doors do not directly face the corridor or EV hall (arrange diagonally) || (Privacy) Avoid tower plans in which balconies of adjacent units face each other at 90 degrees
additional_comment: Secure a corridor width of 1,500mm or more for units designed for persons with disabilities
basis: Regulations on Housing Construction Standards, Article 17 · Design Guideline Article 14 (p. 41)

checklist_item: Verification of stormwater planning adequacy for corridor-access apartments
checkpoints: Plan to avoid interference with the pump box, corridor beam, entrance door leaf, PD access panel, and similar elements || Maintain a spacing of 6~7m between stormwater downspout lines on the residential tower || Verify and improve any obstruction of resident circulation, interference with unit entrance doors, or adverse visual impact
additional_comment: For corridor-access apartments, verify the stormwater plan from the roof through the corridor to the basement drainage channel, and confirm the adequacy of downspout locations

drawing: Building floor plan / Core floor plan
checklist_item: Review of elevator lobby window design in stair-access apartments
checkpoints: A 2m or greater separation from other windows is not required for windows of the stairwell and vestibule (elevator lobby) || Where within 2m of another window, wired glass is not required (as fire compartments are provided every 200㎡ of floor area and the floor area per storey is 400㎡ or less, the stair does not qualify as an evacuation stair or special evacuation stair)
basis: Public Housing Project Office-5386 ('14.11.06) · Enforcement Decree of the Building Act, Article 35

checklist_item: Vibration and noise mitigation planning for units adjacent to elevator shafts
checkpoints: Locate the E/V away from dwelling units so that it does not face them in the tower plan || Where unavoidable, install a double wall or relocate the counterweight away from the units
additional_comment: Locate the E/V away from dwelling units to prevent noise and vibration
basis: Customer Quality Innovation Team-5235 (21.12.02)

checklist_item: Verification of mailbox installation criteria compliance
checkpoints: (Rental) Apply standard mailboxes + smart registered mailbox (integrated type) (install 10% of the units per core at the 1st-floor building entrance) || (Rental) Apply the unmanned parcel delivery system (integrated type) (install 5% of the units per core and control it integrally with the smart registered mailbox) || (For-sale) Apply smart mailboxes / unmanned parcel delivery system (integrated type) (install 15% of the units per core at the 1st-floor building entrance)
basis: Public Housing Facilities Office-545 ('24.02.13.) · Smart Housing Office-3213 ('19.09.08.)

drawing: Building floor plan / Core floor plan
checklist_item: Braille block planning within the apartment complex
checkpoints: Plan braille blocks in the residential tower stairwell from the floor with units for the mobility-impaired down to the 1st floor || Install braille blocks 30cm away from the start and end of stairs || Show them on the overall building floor plan and core plan of the building containing units for the mobility-impaired
basis: Design Guideline Article 14 (p. 40)

drawing: Building floor plan / Core floor plan
checklist_item: Omit vestibule space at roof access
checkpoints: Delete the vestibule space at roof level (retain minimum walls only)
basis: Customer Quality Innovation Team-3130 (`20.07.08.)

drawing: Building floor plan / Auxiliary welfare facilities
checklist_item: Verify stormwater downspout planning criteria
checkpoints: Minimize bends in stormwater downspout connections and avoid exposure on the exterior || Considering the exterior wall stone finish at the ground-floor main entrance canopy and auxiliary welfare facilities, change the downspout material in those areas to stainless steel (STS)
basis: Private-Financed Housing Business Division-1858 ('14.04.04)

checklist_item: Comply with exterior wall molding design criteria
checkpoints: (Rental) Show semi-noncombustible metal molding on the elevation drawing || (For-sale) Show stone molding or semi-noncombustible metal molding on the elevation drawing
basis: Housing Technology Division-2833 ('18.07.26)

checklist_item: Install vertical crack-inducing joints
checkpoints: Install vertical crack-inducing joints in the retaining wall where tall windows (bedrooms 2 and 3) are installed || Joint depth criterion: at least 1/5 of the concrete wall section

drawing: Core floor plan / Auxiliary welfare facilities
checklist_item: Accessible entrance door clearance planning
checkpoints: Clear passage width of entrance doors: 0.9 m or more || Clear distance in front of entrance doors: 1.2 m or more || Where the door is not automatic, secure a maneuvering space of 0.6 m or more beside the entrance door
additional_comment: Where a swing door opens inward, provide a maneuvering space of at least 600 mm beside the entrance so users can step aside as the door opens
other: Eliminate the level difference between the entrance floor and the door threshold (2 cm or less for fire doors); position the door handle grip center 0.8 m to 0.9 m above the floor
basis: Enforcement Rule of the Act on the Promotion of Convenience for Persons with Disabilities, the Elderly, and Pregnant Women, Annex Table 1

checklist_item: Comply with design criteria for fire protection smoke control systems (smoke control dampers)
checkpoints: Fix the location from the basic design stage and install in structural walls (structural wall combined with lightweight partition is prohibited) || Specify the size and location of the automatic pressure differential damper in the drawing notes || Verify the wall opening size (300x1,200) at the automatic pressure differential damper in the E/V shaft || Damper installation height: 1,500 mm from the finished floor to the top of the opening

basis: Customer Quality Innovation Team-3130 ('20.07.08) · Design Guideline Article 14 (p. 33)

checklist_item: E/V sump pit installation
checkpoints: Provide E/V sump pit (600*600*600) and review adequacy of the drainage plan
basis: Housing Cost Management Division-5608 (`16.10.19) · LHCS 14 20 12 10 prefabricated elevator pit formwork

checklist_item: Comply with wall criteria for EPS/TPS rooms in common areas
checkpoints: Provide structural walls and dry PD for the EPS/TPS room (masonry walls are discouraged) || (Corridor-access type) Secure 3.5 m of concrete wall on two or more faces (W2.5m xD1.0m) || (Stair-core type) Secure 3.0 m of concrete wall on two or more faces (W2.0m xD1.0m) || One concrete wall face is acceptable where the minimum length is secured
basis: Customer Quality Innovation Team-5989 (`17.12.27) · Design Guideline Article 14 (p. 48)

drawing: Building elevation / Core floor plan / Auxiliary welfare facilities
checklist_item: Verify stormwater drain material
checkpoints: Verify the stormwater drain material for each location in consideration of exterior wall stone finishes || Apply stainless steel (Φ100 SST'L) at the residential tower canopy and auxiliary welfare facilities || PVC may be applied to stormwater drains on the penthouse roof || Show stormwater pipes on the elevation drawings and the total design
additional_comment: Secure completion quality of the building exterior design
basis: Design Guideline Article 15 (p. 65)

drawing: Core floor plan / Auxiliary welfare facilities
checklist_item: Water sill and railing planning at stairwell ribbon windows
checkpoints: Install a water sill at the bottom of the stairwell ribbon window in the residential tower (terrazzo tile 100x25) || (For-sale) Apply colored galvanized color steel sheet for the railing at the stairwell ribbon window || (Rental) Apply powder coating for the railing at the stairwell ribbon window || Verify railing height of H=1200 from the floor

other: Height of the railing itself is 1100 (100 above the floor)
basis: Customer Quality Innovation Team-6539 ('20.12.16) · Housing Technology Division-2515 (`17.07.06) · DA-70-205

checklist_item: Review adequacy of roof finish and slope
checkpoints: Roof waterproofing: sheet membrane plus THK80 protection concrete (including above the penthouse E/V machine room; show the sheet waterproofing detail at the wall-to-floor junction) || Machine room floor finish: THK100 plain concrete plus epoxy paint (skirting: 80 mm) || Verify roof slope construction (1/50 to 1/150) || Show protection concrete joints at 2,500x2,500 || Railing height: 1,400 mm (structural height)
basis: Design Guideline Article 17 (p. 101) · DA-50-007

checklist_item: Slab thickness and floor-to-floor height planning

basis: Housing Technology Division- · 430 ('19.02.18) · Public For-Sale Business Division-8144 ('23.13.26)

drawing: Main section / Dwelling unit floor plan

drawing: Baseboard and ceiling trim / Dwelling unit floor plan
checklist_item: Review adequacy of in-unit curtain box planning
checkpoints: Verify that the balcony window curtain box in bedrooms does not conflict with built-in closets || Verify that the window curtain box in the dressing room does not conflict with system furniture || Where no other conflict exists, plan the curtain box across the full wall; where conflicts exist, install the curtain box only up to 200 mm beyond the window end
basis: Customer Quality Innovation Team-6399 ('20.12.10)

drawing: Finish construction limit plan / Dwelling unit floor plan
checklist_item: Comply with finish criteria at kitchen cabinet-to-tile junctions
checkpoints: Finish the junction between the kitchen wall tile and the refrigerator cabinet side panel with 10x10 sealant (installing a PVC divider risks complaints due to the gap)
basis: Customer Quality Innovation Team-3130 ('20.07.08)

drawing: Insulation detail / Dwelling unit floor plan
checklist_item: Attach condensation prevention notice
checkpoints: Include attachment of the condensation prevention notice

checklist_item: Verify condensation-reduction material specifications
checkpoints: (Width) In climate zones I and II, the condensation-reduction material width (W) is 450 mm (300 mm in zone III) || (Thickness) Ceiling 15T, wall 13T in all zones || (Material) Ceiling: extruded polystyrene foam (KS M 3808 moisture-proof board type 1) / wall: composite insulation
additional_comment: For built-in closets in adjacent units, the material width used to be increased to match the upper cabinet width; however, with a ceiling-to-slab void there is no condensation impact, so 450 mm is acceptable
basis: DA-60-009 · Design Guideline Article 17 (p. 79) · Design Criteria for Condensation Prevention in Apartment Buildings, Annex Table 1

checklist_item: Comply with design criteria for basement and above-grade residential tower entrance doors
checkpoints: Install system louvers at basement residential tower automatic entrance doors to prevent condensation || Locate the system louver opening/closing lever on the indoor side || Use laminated glass class II-1 or II-2 (laminated glass thickness THK 8.76 or more) || (Above grade) panic automatic door (openable as a swing door), (basement) standard automatic door || Detail the safety sensor position (FL+500~600) and mohair installation
additional_comment: (Laminated glass THK 8.76 or more) THK4 heat-strength glass + THK0.76 or more PVB, EVA or RESIN (liquid resin) + THK4 heat-strength glass, or THK4 tempered glass + THK0.76 or more PVB, EVA or RESIN (liquid resin) + THK4 tempered glass
other: The install area and location of system louvers shall be determined in consideration of ventilation capacity and entrance design
basis: Housing Design Division 2-4517 ('10.11.22) · Housing Technology Division-5434 ('18.12.31) · Housing Technology Division-4739 (`20.12.20) · Design Guideline Article 14 (p. 21) · DA-83-124

checklist_item: Verify window installation criteria for E/V halls
checkpoints: (Shaft pressurization method) Vestibule: sealed windows (only one operable window, with automatic closing device) || (Shaft pressurization method) Stairwell: operable windows on all floors (no automatic closing device) || (ST supply pressurization method) Vestibule: sealed windows (only one operable window, with automatic closing device) || (ST supply pressurization method) Stairwell: sealed windows (one operable window per 5 floors, with automatic closing device)
additional_comment: In corridor-access apartments with shaft supply pressurization smoke control, no ST is provided inside the elevator lobby; install exhaust ST on the side facing the corridor
basis: Design Guideline Article 14 (p. 37)

checklist_item: Insect screen planning for E/V machine room AL windows
checkpoints: Install an aluminum insect screen between the gallery sliding window (exterior) and the glass sliding window (interior) of the E/V machine room window (to prevent equipment failure from insect intrusion)
basis: Customer Quality Innovation Team-4381 ('20.09.07) · DA-95-657 · Design Guideline Article 14 (p. 48)

checklist_item: Verify installation criteria for finger-pinch prevention devices
checkpoints: Where the tallest building in the complex is 16 stories or more, install in every unit || Install finger-pinch prevention material on all interior doors (bedroom, bathroom, utility room doors) || Surface-mounted or integrated type, one set per location (applied to both faces, bedroom side and living room side)
additional_comment: Applies to districts applying for approval after '15.10.28; kitchen turning doors are not legally required but are included in consideration of complaints; apply the same decorative sheet as the door, matching the door leaf height
basis: Housing Technology Division-3969 ('18.10.17) · Housing Technology Division-2893 (`22.07.21) · Criteria for Structural Construction Methods of Interior Architecture, Article 8

checklist_item: Comply with waterproofing method criteria for underground parking garages
checkpoints: Apply exterior waterproofing as the default; where exterior work is difficult, apply interior waterproofing (confined spaces, combined earth retaining wall and basement exterior wall, etc.) || (Exterior waterproofing) Exterior waterproofing layer plus THK13 PP composite panel protection board (protection board: PE protection 10T + polypropylene (PP) surface board 3T) || (Exterior waterproofing) Waterproofing extent: up to 100 mm above the blinding concrete || (Interior waterproofing) Cementitious liquid or cement-blended polymer waterproofing plus wall drainage board || (Interior waterproofing) Apply a waterstop to prevent leakage at the foundation-to-wall joint
additional_comment: For exterior waterproofing, no waterstop is installed between the foundation and the wall
basis: Private-Financed Housing Business Division-571 (`14.01.24.) · Design Center-1568 (`15.05.06.) · Smart Housing Technology Division-124 (`25.01.08) · Design Guideline Article 49 (p. 193) · DA-80-007, 008

checklist_item: Install drainage board at parking garage level-change locations
checkpoints: Provide a wall drainage board at foundation level changes of the parking garage exterior wall where exterior waterproofing is not possible || Take leakage and condensation prevention measures for B1 and B2 parking garages and electrical and mechanical rooms
additional_comment: Electrical and generator rooms must secure an effective ceiling height of 4500 or more, and their floor slabs are set lower than the parking garage slab, creating a level difference
basis: Customer Quality Innovation Team-5917 (`18.11.02.)

drawing: Ramp plan / Ramp elevation / Ramp section
checklist_item: Verify planning of the underground parking ramp entry section
checkpoints: Apply an eave length of 1 m or more at the ramp entrance canopy (600 mm at the sides) || Slope the ramp roof to prevent water ponding and reflect it as a curved roof design || Specify a 1/10 slope toward the exterior at the parking entrance floor || Provide a silent trench where the slope ends
additional_comment: Plan the side and rear roof eave lengths and the finish of the lower open areas to prevent snow and rain intrusion
basis: Customer Quality Innovation Team-5255 ('22.12.05) · Design Guideline Article 42 (p. 176)

checklist_item: Verify planning of the underground parking ramp end section
checkpoints: Provide a safety railing at the parking stalls at the bottom end of the ramp (parallel to the ramp, on both sides of the drive aisle) || Railing: stainless steel, height 1.2 m or more, spacing 10 cm or less || Extend patterned concrete to the driveway at the bottom of the ramp (slip resistance)
additional_comment: Where the parking entrance/exit connects to the main road within the complex, set it back at least 5 m from the main road
basis: Customer Quality Innovation Team-5740 ('18.10.26) · Design Guideline Article 42 (p. 175)

drawing: Underground traffic circulation plan / Ramp plan
checklist_item: Review adequacy of underground parking ramp planning
checkpoints: Straight ramp width 7 m; curved ramp width 7.5 m with a curve radius of 6 m or more || Delete parking stalls at the bottom end of the down ramp (perpendicular to the ramp) || Provide a recognition zone at the ramp end (open structural bay plus structural curb) || Show the center line (solid yellow) and pavement markers on the plan for the ramp section
additional_comment: Plan the main drive aisle with a width of 7 m or more and show curve radii on the drawings so they can be verified
basis: Housing Business Division 2-5477 ('13.09.06) · Customer Quality Innovation Team-5740 ('18.10.26)

checklist_item: Fire compartmentation and fire shutter installation in underground parking garages
checkpoints: Apply fire compartmentation on every floor where two or more basement levels exist, and apply fire shutters || Prohibit integrated fire shutters with a door opening within part of the shutter || Install a fire shutter at the ramp end and provide a separate fire door in the side structural wall || Avoid parking stalls in front of fire doors in consideration of evacuation routes in disasters
additional_comment: Fire compartment relaxation may be granted only where the ramp and aisles of the underground parking garage are compartmented from other parts of the building; the portion directly connecting B1 to the ground floor need not be compartmented (per floor or between floors is acceptable)
basis: MOLIT Notice No. 2020-44 ('20.1.30)

drawing: Ramp plan / Ramp front elevation / Underground parking floor plan
checklist_item: Review adequacy of ramp entry and exit planning for the underground parking garage
checkpoints: Secure a minimum ramp and aisle height of 2.7m to avoid overhead interference when delivery vehicles enter || Mark height limits at the ground-level ramp entrance: vehicle aisle 2.7m, parking space 2.5m || Where a lower-clearance level exists, apply that restricted height (vehicle aisle 2.3m, parking space 2.1m) || Install a speed hump at the crossing point, 3m clear of the bottom end of the ramp || Indicate convex mirrors at blind spots such as parking ramps and curved sections of site roads
basis: Customer Quality Innovation Group-5740 ('18.10.26) · Design Guideline Article 42 (p.176)

checklist_item: Compliance with parking layout criteria for the underground parking garage
checkpoints: Secure a main aisle width of 7m and other aisle widths of 6m or more || Verify accessible parking markings (planned identically above and below grade) || Plan skylights and artificial drainage pipes in the driving zone (carriageway area) || Plan 1 wheel stopper (L=600mm) for each standard parking stall || At parking garage corners, space the parking lines so vehicles can park on both sides || Configure parking spaces with turnaround allowance for dead-end areas || Locate underground facility entrances so they do not adjoin the carriageway
additional_comment: Considering typical vehicle speeds on ramps (20~30km), a stopping distance of 8~9m is required; delete 2~3 parking stalls at the bottom of the down ramp

drawing: Residential tower plan / Underground parking floor plan
checklist_item: Review adequacy of parking planned inside apartment PIT levels
checkpoints: Adjust the parking supply to avoid parking stalls inside the PIT || Where PIT parking is unavoidable, plan compact-car stalls to secure pedestrian circulation || Plan so that door swing does not interfere with columns or walls
additional_comment: (Rahmen) The distance from the front of the parking stall to the column face must be within 1,350mm for occupants to get in and out. (Flat plate) Because of the column size, a distance of 1,500mm from the front of the stall to the column face still satisfies the door-opening criterion.
other: Where a parking area abuts a wall or a column sits near the side mirror, doors cannot be opened; review and revise
basis: Customer Quality Innovation Group-6097 ('18.11.12) · Design Guideline Article 42 (p.172)

drawing: Residential tower plan / Underground parking floor plan
checklist_item: Review adequacy of accessible parking zone planning
checkpoints: Secure a passage from the underground accessible parking zone to the entrance || Provide the pedestrian safety path with a clear width of 1.2m or more, separated from the vehicle aisle || Secure the code-required aisle width (6m or more) in the parking garage, excluding the safety path || Distinguish floor material and color and show them on the drawings || Plan 2 wheel stoppers (L=600mm) for each accessible parking stall
additional_comment: Avoid parking stalls in front of entrances so the passage to the residential tower entrance is not blocked
basis: Enforcement Rule of the Housing Vulnerable Support Act, Table 1 · Customer Quality Innovation Group-5738 ('18.10.26)

checklist_item: Review adequacy of flat-plate underground parking garage planning
checkpoints: For flat-plate underground parking garages, the standard module is 2 cars with a 1-way slab || Where the module exceeds 2 cars, verify structural capacity together with the structural discipline || Do not allow risers or skylights to penetrate the column strip of the 450mm slab
additional_comment: Flat-plate design must always be determined in consultation with the structural discipline

checklist_item: Review adequacy of safety facilities and graphics for the underground parking garage
checkpoints: Plan a safe pedestrian/vehicle circulation system through floor graphics in the underground parking garage || Show vehicle circulation, conflict zones, ramp centerlines, exit guidance markings, and painted speed humps || Mark compact-car stalls with a solid blue line (mandatory) plus a separate graphic design (recommended)
basis: Design Guideline Article 42 (p.172) · Design Guideline Article 46 (p.189)

drawing: Underground parking floor plan / Electrical generator room plan
checklist_item: Confirmation of trench and sump planning in the underground parking garage
checkpoints: In principle, do not install trenches in the underground parking garage || Install them at entrance ramps, basement spaces such as the electrical and mechanical rooms, and open-air deck parking || Where the electrical room, generator room, etc. are fire-compartmented per room, do not link rooms with open trenches || Provide a separate sump for the electrical room and the generator room || Where a sump is installed in an open location, install a fence to prevent access to the pumps
additional_comment: Trenches may be installed depending on site conditions; use silent-type trenches at the underground parking entrance ramp, and open or PC trenches in mechanical/electrical equipment spaces and deck-type parking
basis: Housing Technology Division-2379 ('18.06.27) · Design Guideline Article 49 (p.192) · DA-76-015 · DA-76-016

drawing: Residential tower plan / Underground parking floor plan
checklist_item: Compliance with criteria for the number of sumps
checkpoints: Determine trench and sump locations considering the drain-down pipe positions of risers || Install 1 sump for combinations of 6 dwellings or fewer, and 2 for 6-dwelling (L-shaped) combinations and combinations of 7 dwellings or more || Where a sump is provided to drain the elevator shaft floor, review whether it can be combined with the residential tower basement sump || Install sumps with a diameter of 450mm or more and a depth of 600mm or more
basis: DA-76-011~014 · Design Guideline Article 14 (p.46)

drawing: Underground parking floor plan / Underground parking section
checklist_item: Compliance with floor finish criteria for the underground parking garage
checkpoints: (Solvent-free epoxy coating) Parking stalls in the underground parking garage (excluding accessible parking stalls) || (Solvent-free epoxy embossed) Carriageway areas and accessible parking in the underground parking garage (excluding ramp areas) || (Patterned concrete + floor hardener) Ramps, the horizontal run below the ramps, and turning areas || (Epoxy coating) Electrical room, generator room, pump room, storage, fan room || (Steel trowel finish) Water tank, PIT floor
additional_comment: For the underground parking garage floor and the ramp floor, place unreinforced concrete (25-24-150); for the protective layer over waterproofing on the underground parking garage top slab, place topping concrete (25-18-150)
other: Delete the PIT floor waterproofing (cement liquid waterproofing + protective mortar) and apply a steel trowel finish
basis: Customer Quality Innovation Group-4276 ('19.07.17) · Design Guideline Article 49 (p.195) · Design Verification Division-7850 ('24.12.04)

drawing: Exterior stair plan / Exterior stair section
checklist_item: Confirmation of floor finish planning for outdoor stair towers
checkpoints: Apply granite bush-hammered finish to the floor of outdoor stair towers serving the underground parking garage || Provide a floor level difference (GL+150) || Plan the structure to prevent snow, rain, snowmelt, and water ingress

checklist_item: Measures to prevent stormwater inflow below ventilation openings
checkpoints: Secure concrete curb height to prevent stormwater inflow, allowing for planting mounds || Minimum H=300 from the finished grade to the bottom frame of the DA ventilation opening || Apply appropriate stormwater inflow prevention measures reflecting actual site conditions
basis: DA-80-201, DA-83-202~204 · Customer Quality Innovation Group-2458 ('22.06.28)

checklist_item: Review adequacy of parking planning for EV charging facilities
checkpoints: Install EV charging facilities for at least 10% of total parking spaces (`25 basis) || Distinguish fast chargers (count per local government ordinance) from slow chargers (all remaining spaces) || Locate where adjacent to outdoor air, exclude levels below basement 3, and keep 10m from major facilities
additional_comment: For surface parking, keep 10m from buildings and 20m from playgrounds, daycare centers, and combustible storage; exclude areas near landscaped facilities and locate where fire trucks can gain access
other: (Major facilities) Residential tower entrances, areas around evacuation routes, electrical rooms, waste storage areas
basis: Public Housing Facility Division-69 ('25.01.06)

drawing: Underground utilities composite plan / Residential tower plan / Residential tower elevation
checklist_item: Planning of underground parking garage ventilation openings and PIT ventilation windows
checkpoints: (Basement 1) Where the ventilation opening area is less than 1/40 of the floor area, apply Type 3 ventilation (natural supply, mechanical exhaust), preferably with openings along the carriageway and around stair towers || (Basement 2 and below) Apply Type 1 ventilation (mechanical supply and exhaust), with supply and exhaust ducts passing through the first floor and discharging to the rooftop ventilation tower || (PIT ventilation window) 1 per dwelling per basement level, staggered, located within the open span of the typical-floor wall || Where a step-free design makes PIT ventilation windows infeasible, review mechanical ventilation of the PIT || (PIT ventilation window size) For-sale: PW 12x4 / corridor-access type: PW 12x3 || Confirm consistency with the overall plan and the structural drawings
basis: Design Guideline Articles 14 and 44 (pp.45, 187)

checklist_item: Compliance with installation criteria for worker rest facilities
checkpoints: Residential complexes of 50 dwellings or more must provide worker rest facilities || Minimum area 6㎡, ceiling height 2.1m or more, separate rooms for men and women || Kitchen, toilet including a shower, heating and cooling, humidity and lighting control || Shoe cabinet, storage cabinet, and other furnishings
additional_comment: Locate at grade where possible for convenient use and good ventilation
basis: Regulations on Housing Construction Standards, Article 28 · Occupational Safety and Health Act, Article 128-2

checklist_item: Compliance with planning criteria for the security office
checkpoints: Install the security office at an appropriate size facing the direction of vehicle entry (including office, toilet, and pantry) || Plan building position and window orientation so that gateposts, building corners, etc. do not obstruct sightlines || Show gateposts and complex entrances on the security office floor plan so the viewing angle can be verified || Secure additional space for storing parcels

checklist_item: Compliance with installation criteria for the community care center
checkpoints: Mandatory in housing complexes of 500 dwellings or more (approval applications filed after '21.1.12) || Provide a dedicated area of at least 66㎡ || Provide a play area or activity room, office space, toilet, and cooking area separately
additional_comment: In addition to the daycare center, complexes of 500 dwellings or more must install a community care center. Where the approving authority judges installation unnecessary in view of the complex's characteristics and nearby provision, it may be omitted
basis: Regulations on Housing Construction Standards, Article 55-2

checklist_item: Compliance with planning criteria for the daycare center
checkpoints: Plan the daycare center area at a minimum of 4.29㎡ per child || Secure space for a washing machine in the toilet, or add detailed plumbing to a separately partitioned laundry room (water supply and drainage) || Eliminate floor level differences at the daycare entrance and the hallway (20mm or less where unavoidable) || Install exterior windows at 60~70cm height so children can look outside
additional_comment: When planning the daycare center, secure ventilation and daylight for staff rooms and childcare rooms, and provide a separate food supply entrance for the kitchen
basis: Customer Quality Innovation Group-6446 ('20.12.14) · Enforcement Rule of the Housing Vulnerable Support Act, Table 1 · Design Guideline Article 31 (p.143) · DA-92-107

checklist_item: Confirmation of safety planning for the daycare center
checkpoints: Install child-height handrails on daycare stairs, corridors, and ramps || Install the child handrail as a double handrail separate from the adult handrail || Plan all doors as pocket sliding doors with tempered glass in the upper and lower panels || Install anti-pinch devices (dampers, etc.) on doors (childcare rooms, toilets, vestibule intermediate doors) || Provide a bottom rail at exterior windows of daycare playrooms to prevent collisions and other accidents
basis: Design Guideline Article 31 (p.149) · Customer Quality Innovation Group-4354 ('20.09.04)

checklist_item: Review of barrier-free planning for auxiliary welfare facilities
checkpoints: Where BF certification applies, confirm the adequacy of barrier-free spaces || Apply the criteria to access paths, accessible parking zones, entrances, corridors, stairs, sanitary facilities, guest rooms, etc. || Coordinate pedestrian paths, complex levels, ramps, and tactile blocks among the architecture, landscape, and civil disciplines || Plan the walking route across the accessible parking zone as level ground || Reflect tactile blocks on crosswalks outside the site, aligned with the direction of travel || Confirm the review results for non-compliance with the Act on Convenience Facilities for Persons with Disabilities
basis: Article 10-2 of the Housing Vulnerable Support Act · Article 2 and Table 5 of the Barrier-Free (BF) Certification Review Criteria and Fee Standards

checklist_item: Planning of accessible toilets in auxiliary welfare facilities
checkpoints: Provide at least one accessible toilet stall for men and one for women || Accessible toilet clear floor area: width 1.6m, depth 2.0m || Provide 0.75m clear space for transfer on the left or right side of the toilet || Provide wheelchair turning space in front of the toilet (1.4x1.4m) || Door clear opening width of 0.9m or more
additional_comment: Refer to Table 1 of the Enforcement Rule of the Act on Convenience Promotion for Persons with Disabilities, the Elderly, and Pregnant Women
basis: Design Guideline Article 31 (p.156) · Table 1 of the Act on Convenience Facilities for Persons with Disabilities

checklist_item: Confirmation of wind lobby planning criteria for auxiliary welfare facilities
checkpoints: Plan a wind lobby at entrances directly exposed to outdoor air and connected to the first floor or grade (may be omitted for doors with width W=1.2m or less) || Where the distance between the inner and outer doors of the wind lobby is 3m or more, install tactile dot blocks inside and outside (may be omitted inside where the distance is under 3m)
basis: Customer Quality Innovation Group-6399 ('20.12.10)

drawing: Auxiliary welfare facility plan / Auxiliary welfare facility window schedule
checklist_item: Confirmation of window planning criteria for auxiliary welfare facilities
checkpoints: Avoid project windows in auxiliary welfare facilities and use sliding windows (if project windows are used, create planting space around them to prevent collisions, considering pedestrian circulation) || For daycare centers and senior centers (other than neighborhood living facilities), use synthetic resin windows || For neighborhood living facilities, use metal windows with thermal breaks || Thermal transmittance of 1.5 or less and airtightness class 1 or better (common to all windows)
basis: Customer Quality Innovation Group-4645 (2021.11.01) · Design Guideline Article 26 (p.132)

checklist_item: Compliance with railing installation criteria for auxiliary welfare facilities
checkpoints: Install glass railings with laminated glass THK 11.52 or thicker, type Ⅱ-1 or Ⅱ-2 || For stair railings, provide a height of 1,200mm or more with baluster spacing of 100mm or less
basis: Design Guideline Articles 14 and 26 (pp.35, 133)

drawing: Auxiliary welfare facility plan / Auxiliary welfare facility window schedule
checklist_item: Confirmation of adequacy of door planning for auxiliary welfare facilities
checkpoints: Door clear width (SSD, SD, AD) of 900mm or more, frame width 1100mm or more || Install anti-pinch devices on doors (SSD) at the frame and the handle || No thermal insulation performance for interior room-to-room windows (SSD) in auxiliary welfare facilities (fixed window (SSD): upper THK5 float glass, lower THK10 tempered glass) || Apply opaque glass to doors of the fitness shower room and auxiliary facility toilets
additional_comment: Interior room-to-room windows omit thermal performance in consideration of breakage and privacy
basis: Customer Quality Innovation Group-3130 ('20.07.08) · Customer Quality Innovation Group-6399 ('20.12.10) · DA-98-125

checklist_item: Application of fire compartment separation to facilities facing the underground parking garage
checkpoints: Where auxiliary welfare facilities, seasonal storage, etc. face the underground parking garage, separate them as a fire compartment (apply fire doors (FSD, FSSD, etc.) to adjacent auxiliary welfare facility entrances; SD not permitted)
basis: Customer Quality Innovation Group-6399 ('20.12.10)

drawing: Interior finish schedule / Interior finish detail
checklist_item: Compliance with ceiling frame criteria for auxiliary welfare facilities
checkpoints: For lightweight steel ceiling frames with a ceiling depth of 1.5m or more, apply minor channels (at 1.8m spacing both ways) || Where the toilet or shower ceiling area exceeds 3㎡, apply PVC ceiling panels (ABS panels otherwise)
basis: Housing Technology Division-3784 ('20.11.2) · Customer Quality Innovation Group-6399 ('20.12.10) · DA-32-001~003

drawing: Auxiliary welfare facility elevation / Exterior report
checklist_item: Confirmation of stormwater handling planning for auxiliary welfare facilities
checkpoints: Slope the roofs of auxiliary facilities toward the roof drains || Use STS for downspout receivers, considering appearance and usability || At sunken areas, plan auxiliary facility entrances with a level difference, waterproofing curb, or trench
basis: Site Quality Management Division-3048 ('14.12.08) · Design Guideline Article 15 (p.65)
